fields.label: Dust Particle Concentration (kg dust/m<sup>3</sup> air)
fields.help: Enter the concentration of dust particles in the air compartments. The default value of 6.15E-08 is from Bidleman, T.F. 1988. Atmospheric processes. Environmental Science and Technology 22:361-367

fields.label: Density of Air (g/cm<sup>3</sup>)
fields.help: Enter the density of air in the air compartments. The default value of 0.0012 (1.12E-03) is from Table B-1 of U.S. EPA (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency). 1997. Mercury Study Report to Congress. Volume III: Fate and Transport of Mercury in the Environment. EPA-452/R-97-005. Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards and Office of Research and Development. December. Available online at: https://www3.epa.gov/ttn/atw/112nmerc/volume3.pdf.

fields.label: Density of Dust Particles (kg/cm<sup>3</sup>)
fields.help: Enter the density of dust particles in the air compartments. The default value of 1400 (1.4 g/cm<sup>3</sup>) is from Page 2 of Bidleman, T.F. 1988. Atmospheric processes. Environmental Science and Technology 22:361-367

fields.label: Fraction Organic Matter of Dust Particles
fields.help: Enter the fraction organic matter of dust particles in the air compartments. The default value of 0.2 is from Harner, T., and Bidleman, T.F. 1998. Octanol-air partition coefficient for describing particle/gas partitioning of aromatic compounds in urban air. Environmental Science and Technology 32:1494‑1502.

fields.label: Surface Soil Tilled Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of a tilled layer of surface soil. The default value of 0.20 is from Human Health Risk Assessment Protocol for Hazardous Waste Combustion Facilities (including the Hazardous Waste Companion Database of chemical-specific parameter values). U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Solid Waste and Emergency Response, Washington, DC. EPA-530-R-05-006. September. Available online at: https://archive.epa.gov/epawaste/hazard/tsd/td/web/html/risk.html.

fields.label: Surface Soil Untilled Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of an untilled layer of surface soil. The default value of 0.01 is from p. 30 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk..

fields.label: Root Soil Tilled Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of a tilled layer of root-zone soil. The default value of 0.60 assumes that the total thickness of the surface-soil layer and root-zone layer is 0.8 (0.01 for untilled surface soil [from p. 30 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk.] + 0.79 for untilled root zone [from Table 16 - U.S. Average from McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk]). If the thickness of a tilled surface soil layer is 0.2 (from Human Health Risk Assessment Protocol for Hazardous Waste Combustion Facilities (including the Hazardous Waste Companion Database of chemical-specific parameter values). U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Solid Waste and Emergency Response, Washington, DC. EPA-530-R-05-006. September. Available online at: https://archive.epa.gov/epawaste/hazard/tsd/td/web/html/risk.html.), then the thickness of a tilled root zone is 0.8 - 0.2 = 0.6.

fields.label: Root Soil Untilled Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of an untilled layer of root-zone soil. The default value of 0.79 is from p. 30 of McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk.

fields.label: Vadose Zone Soil Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of the vadose zone. The default value of 1.4 is from Tabel 17 - U.S. Average from McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk.

fields.label: Groundwater Thickness (m)
fields.help: Enter the thickness of the groundwater layer. The default value of 3 is from Tabel 3 - Thickness of the aquifer layer from McKone, T.E., A. Bodnar, and E. Hertwich. 2001. Development and evaluation of state-specific landscape data sets for multimedia source-to-dose models. University of California at Berkeley. Supported by U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Sustainable Technology Division, National Risk Management Research Laboratory) and Environmental Defense Fund. July. LBNL-43722. Available online at: https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9f1164rk.
